page.title: How pagination works
page.snippet: List endpoints return a page of objects and a has_more flag. To get the next page, pass the id of the last object as starting_after. Use ending_before to page backwards. limit sets the page size.

page.snippet: Every response includes x-ratelimit-limit, x-ratelimit-remaining and x-ratelimit-reset headers. When x-ratelimit-remaining reaches 0, wait until the time in x-ratelimit-reset before retrying.

e7_duplicates.query: How do I paginate results in the Stripe API?

page_a.title: How pagination works
page_a.snippet: To get the next page of a list, pass the id of the last object you received as starting_after. has_more tells you whether more objects exist.

page_b.title: Paging through Stripe lists
page_b.snippet: Stripe uses cursor pagination: send starting_after set to the last object's id to fetch the following page, and keep going while has_more is true.

e7_duplicates.query: How do I do an upsert in PostgreSQL?

page_a.title: INSERT
page_a.snippet: Use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (column) DO UPDATE SET ... to update the existing row instead of raising a unique violation.

page_b.title: Postgres upsert explained
page_b.snippet: An upsert in Postgres is written INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (col) DO UPDATE SET, which updates the row that already exists rather than failing on the unique constraint.

e7_duplicates.query: How do I make Docker detect that my container has stopped responding?

page_a.title: HEALTHCHECK
page_a.snippet: Add a HEALTHCHECK CMD instruction to the Dockerfile. Docker runs the command on an interval and marks the container unhealthy after the configured retries.

page_b.title: Docker health checks
page_b.snippet: Put HEALTHCHECK CMD in your Dockerfile; Docker executes it periodically and flags the container as unhealthy once it fails the set number of retries.
